segments.text: This worm eats whale bones — and it doesn't even have a mouth.
Found in 2002, growing straight out of a dead whale's skeleton. Nobody had seen anything like it.
No gut. No stomach. Not even an anus. This thing shouldn't be able to eat anything.
Turns out it doesn't need to. Its roots drill straight into the bone, dump acid, and let bacteria inside it do the actual eating.
And the males? They never grow up. Hundreds of them, microscopic, living inside one female for her entire life.
It's not even picky about whales. Scientists dropped cow bones on the sea floor — same worms showed up in months.
Whale, cow, whatever sinks — something down there is already waiting to eat it.
